subject: Electrical Engineering
title: TCP/IP: The Internet's Protocol Stack
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: TCP/IP: The Internet's Protocol Stack.

hook.text: TCP/IP is the protocol suite that runs the internet. Every device online speaks it.

buildup.text: IP handles addressing and routing. TCP handles reliable, ordered delivery of data streams.

discovery.text: TCP uses acknowledgments and retransmissions — if a packet is lost, it sends it again automatically.

twist.text: UDP skips reliability for speed — no acknowledgments, no retransmission. Perfect for live video and gaming.

climax.text: HTTP, email, DNS, and streaming all ride on TCP/IP — the common language of all connected devices.

punchline.text: IP routes, TCP delivers — two protocols underpin everything on the internet.

quiz.question: Why would a video streaming service choose UDP over TCP?
options: UDP provides better security through encryption
UDP skips retransmission for lower latency — a dropped frame matters less than delay
UDP compresses video data more efficiently
